thread:
tom: Noticed the canary got ~30% traffic even though we set it to 5% this morning. Anyone else seeing weird split math?

devops-bot: Deploy triggered: canary rollout v2 -> 5% at 2026-02-14T09:12:30Z :white_check_mark:

alana: I saw this too, but only from a subset of clients. Looks correlated with header-based routing rules.

riyad: Can you paste an example request header that hit the canary?

alana: Here's an anonymized one from logs: `Host: api.redwood.test`, `User-Agent: curl/7.82`, `X-RW-Region: eu-west-1`, `X-Client-Id: 0000abCDef`. It hit canary.

alex: Replaying a few from the same client id locally — the hash we use for splits lowercases the client id, but if the header has mixed case the routing layer was reading it as-is. I think case-sensitivity caused the murmur3 bucket to jump ranges.

sophie: That's the sticky cookie path too, right? Cookies are set using `session_id` but some clients send `Session-ID` because of a proxy. If we don't normalize, the sticky lookup misses and we fall back to header-hash which is inconsistent.

tom: So two things: header normalization + consistent key for sticky sessions. Any easy fix we can push to stop the bleed?

alex: Quick mitigation: set canary to 0% via console and rollback rollout. But that doesn't fix the root cause.

devops-bot: Action executed: set rollout v2 -> 0% at 2026-02-14T09:25:04Z :warning:

riyad: For a proper fix we should canonicalize header names and cookie keys at the router ingress (lowercase) and also use a normalized salt string in hash computation. Proposed patch diff:

```
# router/route_hash.go (concept)
func normalizeKey(k string) string { return strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(k)) }
hashKey := normalizeKey(header.Get("X-Client-Id")) + ":" + route.Salt
```

alana: Also add a fallback: if sticky cookie present but different case, try both `session_id` and `Session-ID` before computing the hash. Add telemetry metric `routing.sticky_key_mismatch`.

alex: I dug into telemetry — there are ~12k requests in last hour where `routing.bucket` is unset but `routing.fallback_hash`=true. That matches the surge.

riyad: Tests: add unit tests for header cases and an e2e that injects a proxy which mangles header casing. Will open PR with tests + router normalizer.

tom: Sounds good. Who wants to own the PR and the follow-up console change to expose a normalized view in the rollout UI? (Right now UI shows the raw header rule.)

alana: I'll take the PR (small changes).

alex: I'll do the UI bits — update the rollout preview to show canonicalized matching key and a note about sticky lookup order.

sophie: I'll add an alert: `canary.traffic.delta > 10% expected` tied to `routing.bucket_distribution` so we get paged if splits diverge.

devops-bot: Created issue RW-PLT-423: header normalization + sticky fallback. Assigned to alana/alex/sophie.

tom: Thanks. Plan: rollback was done, monitor for any residual drift. Alana — aim to have PR by EOD. Sophie — alert and dashboard tweak?

alana: PR opened: https://git.redwood/s/alana/router-header-normalize (includes tests).

alex: UI PR draft up: https://git.redwood/s/alex/rollout-ui-normalize. Preview shows canonical header key.

sophie: Alert rule added to staging. Will promote to prod after PR merge.

riyad: Once merged, we should rerun a small canary (1%) and watch `routing.sticky_key_mismatch` -> expecting near-zero.

tom: Great. Lesson: header/cookie casing can leak traffic out of guarded buckets. Thanks team :thumbsup:
